section: Indian industry - structure, growth and contribution; IIP; public sector role and performance
subsections: Public sector enterprise categories - Maharatna, Navratna, Miniratna criteria, company status, numbers, financial autonomy

accepted.s: A Central Public Sector Enterprise (CPSE) is a company in which the Central Government or other CPSEs directly hold at least what percentage of the equity capital?
accepted.x: A CPSE is a company in which the Central Government or other CPSEs directly hold 51% or more.
accepted.tq: Use the precise ownership threshold to distinguish a CPSE from other public-sector-associated companies.
accepted.sec: Public sector enterprise categories - Maharatna, Navratna, Miniratna criteria, company status, numbers, financial autonomy  [APPSC]

accepted.s: The principal purpose of conferring Maharatna, Navratna and Miniratna status on high-performing CPSEs is to provide them with:
o: automatic budgetary support from the Government
accepted.x: The ratna categories grant high-performing CPSEs greater financial and operational autonomy, including the ability to invest, form joint ventures and compete globally with fewer approvals.
accepted.tq: Identify the objective of a policy rather than confusing autonomy with exemption or guaranteed budgetary support.
accepted.sec: Public sector enterprise categories - Maharatna, Navratna, Miniratna criteria, company status, numbers, financial autonomy  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the Maharatna scheme:
1. A company must already possess Navratna status to become eligible for Maharatna status.
2. The scheme was introduced in 2009 and the first grants were made in 2010.
3. A Maharatna CPSE may invest up to ₹5,000 crore in a single project without prior Government approval.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three statements are correct. Maharatna eligibility requires existing Navratna status, the scheme was introduced in 2009 with first grants in 2010, and investment autonomy extends up to ₹5,000 crore in one project.
accepted.tq: Check each eligibility, date and financial-limit statement separately before selecting the coded combination.
accepted.sec: Public sector enterprise categories - Maharatna, Navratna, Miniratna criteria, company status, numbers, financial autonomy  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT a stated eligibility condition for Maharatna status?
o: Three-year average net worth exceeding ₹15,000 crore
Three-year average net profit exceeding ₹5,000 crore
Profit in each of the last three years and pre-tax profit of at least ₹30 crore in one year
accepted.x: Profit in each of the last three years and pre-tax profit of at least ₹30 crore in one year are Miniratna Category-I conditions. Maharatna conditions include the specified turnover, net worth, net profit, listing, Navratna status and global presence.
accepted.tq: Find the criterion belonging to a neighbouring category rather than to Maharatna.
accepted.sec: Public sector enterprise categories - Maharatna, Navratna, Miniratna criteria, company status, numbers, financial autonomy  [APPSC]

accepted.s: Which of the following combinations correctly represents the three-year average financial thresholds for Maharatna eligibility?
o: Turnover ₹25,000 crore, net worth ₹5,000 crore and net profit ₹15,000 crore
Turnover ₹25,000 crore, net worth ₹15,000 crore and net profit ₹5,000 crore
Turnover ₹15,000 crore, net worth ₹25,000 crore and net profit ₹5,000 crore
Turnover ₹5,000 crore, net worth ₹15,000 crore and net profit ₹25,000 crore
accepted.x: Maharatna eligibility requires a three-year average turnover above ₹25,000 crore, net worth above ₹15,000 crore and net profit above ₹5,000 crore.
accepted.tq: Match each financial figure with the correct indicator instead of merely recalling the three numbers.
accepted.sec: Public sector enterprise categories - Maharatna, Navratna, Miniratna criteria, company status, numbers, financial autonomy  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
With reference to Navratna CPSEs, consider the following statements:
1. The Navratna scheme was introduced in 1997.
2. An eligible enterprise should be a Miniratna-I and a Schedule 'A' company.
3. It should have an Excellent or Very Good MoU rating in three out of five years.
4. It should secure a score of at least 60 on six parameters.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All four statements correctly state the conditions listed for Navratna eligibility: introduction in 1997, Miniratna-I and Schedule 'A' status, the MoU performance requirement and the six-parameter score of 60 or more.
accepted.tq: Use the all-inclusive option only after verifying every component of a multi-condition eligibility test.
accepted.sec: Public sector enterprise categories - Maharatna, Navratna, Miniratna criteria, company status, numbers, financial autonomy  [APPSC]

accepted.s: A Navratna CPSE may make investment without prior Government approval up to:
o: ₹300 crore or 50% of net worth, whichever is lower
₹1,000 crore or 15% of its net worth, whichever is lower
₹500 crore or its net worth, whichever is lower
accepted.x: Navratna financial autonomy permits investment up to ₹1,000 crore or 15% of net worth, whichever is lower.
accepted.tq: Separate the investment limits of Navratna and the two Miniratna categories by category-specific figures.

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II regarding CPSE categories and their investment autonomy.

List-I (Category)
a. Maharatna
a. Navratna
c. Miniratna-I
d. Miniratna-II

List-II (Limit)
i. Up to ₹300 crore or 50% of net worth
 ii. Up to ₹5,000 crore in one project
 iii. Up to ₹500 crore or equal to net worth
 iv. Up to ₹1,000 crore or 15% of net worth

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
accepted.x: Maharatna corresponds to ₹5,000 crore in one project; Navratna to ₹1,000 crore or 15% of net worth; Miniratna-I to ₹500 crore or equal to net worth; and Miniratna-II to ₹300 crore or 50% of net worth.
accepted.tq: Start from the distinctive Maharatna limit and then eliminate codes using the Miniratna limits.

accepted.s: Which one of the following is the correct distinction between Miniratna Category-I and Miniratna Category-II?
o: Category-I requires Navratna status, whereas Category-II requires Maharatna status.
Category-I requires global presence, whereas Category-II requires listing on a stock exchange.
Category-I and Category-II have identical eligibility conditions but different names.

Category-I requires three consecutive years of profit, ₹30 crore pre-tax profit in at least one year and positive net worth; Category-II requires three consecutive years of profit and positive net worth.
accepted.x: Miniratna-I requires profits in the last three consecutive years, pre-tax profit of at least ₹30 crore in at least one year and positive net worth. Miniratna-II requires profits for three consecutive years and positive net worth.
accepted.tq: Focus on the additional ₹30 crore pre-tax-profit condition that separates Miniratna-I from Miniratna-II.
accepted.sec: Public sector enterprise categories - Maharatna, Navratna, Miniratna criteria, company status, numbers, financial autonomy  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Arrange the following schemes in chronological order of their introduction:
A. Maharatna scheme
B. Navratna scheme
C. Miniratna scheme

Select the correct answer using the code given below:
accepted.x: Navratna and Miniratna were introduced in 1997, while the Maharatna scheme was introduced in 2009. Thus, the sequence is Navratna, Miniratna, Maharatna.
accepted.tq: Place the two 1997 schemes together and use the later 2009 introduction to fix the final position.

accepted.s: The Navratna scheme was initially introduced for how many public sector enterprises?
accepted.x: The Navratna scheme was introduced in 1997 for the first nine public sector enterprises.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the original number of Navratna enterprises from later category counts.

accepted.s: The authority responsible for granting Maharatna, Navratna and Miniratna status to CPSEs is the:
o: Securities and Exchange Board of India
accepted.x: The Department of Public Enterprises grants the ratna status to eligible CPSEs. It is now under the Ministry of Finance.
accepted.tq: Apply the 'who grants the status?' approach and distinguish the administrative authority from regulatory bodies.
accepted.sec: Public sector enterprise categories - Maharatna, Navratna, Miniratna criteria, company status, numbers, financial autonomy  [APPSC]

accepted.s: At present, the Department of Public Enterprises functions under which Ministry?
accepted.x: The Department of Public Enterprises is now under the Ministry of Finance. Older administrative references placed it under the Ministry of Heavy Industries and Public Enterprises.
accepted.tq: Watch for the old-versus-current ministry trap in questions on administrative departments.

accepted.s: As on 1 April 2025, the number of Maharatna and Navratna CPSEs was respectively:
accepted.x: As on 1 April 2025, there were 14 Maharatna and 26 Navratna CPSEs. The current Miniratna count is not specified here.
accepted.tq: Read the date and preserve the order of the two categories while separating current counts from historical figures.

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched with reference to the status of CPSEs?
o: HAL — Maharatna; Bharat Electronics Limited — Navratna
HAL — Navratna; Bharat Electronics Limited — Maharatna
HAL — Miniratna Category-I; Bharat Electronics Limited — Navratna
HAL — Maharatna; Bharat Electronics Limited — Miniratna Category-II
accepted.x: HAL is a Maharatna CPSE, while Bharat Electronics Limited is a Navratna CPSE; BEL received Navratna status in June 2007.
accepted.tq: Use paired company-status matching to avoid reversing adjacent ratna categories.

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding the conditions applicable to all ratna categories:
1. The enterprise should not receive budgetary support.
2. The enterprise should not have a Government guarantee.
3. The enterprise should not be in default on Government loans.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: All three are common conditions for the ratna categories: no budgetary support, no Government guarantee and no default on Government loans.
accepted.tq: Test common conditions separately from category-specific eligibility requirements.
accepted.sec: Public sector enterprise categories - Maharatna, Navratna, Miniratna criteria, company status, numbers, financial autonomy  [APPSC]

accepted.s:
Assertion (A): Ratna status is granted to selected CPSEs on the basis of financial performance.
Reason (R): The status is intended to provide such enterprises with greater financial and operational autonomy.
o: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
accepted.x: Both the Assertion and Reason are true. However, the purpose of granting autonomy explains the benefit of ratna status, not the fact that the status is granted specifically on the basis of financial performance.
accepted.tq: Separate the basis for granting a status from the purpose served by that status.
accepted.sec: Public sector enterprise categories - Maharatna, Navratna, Miniratna criteria, company status, numbers, financial autonomy  [APPSC]

accepted.s: A CPSE is seeking to approve an investment of ₹4,500 crore in a single project without prior Government approval. Which status, subject to fulfilment of other conditions, provides the relevant investment autonomy?
accepted.x: Maharatna CPSEs may approve investments up to ₹5,000 crore in one project without prior Government approval. The stated limits for Navratna and Miniratna enterprises are lower.
accepted.tq: Compare the numerical autonomy limits and identify the category capable of handling the stated project.
